summary: Firestore and Storage use default-deny rules, strict ownership and validation. Administrative authorization relies on a backend-managed custom claim. Account deletion is implemented as an App Check-protected callable function, and RevenueCat Premium state is synchronized by an authenticated, idempotent webhook.

findings.result: Rules require request.auth.token.admin == true. An email address alone grants no backend access.
The callable deletes data only for request.auth.uid and requires App Check plus authentication no older than five minutes.
The RevenueCat webhook authenticates requests, rejects duplicate event IDs and prevents stale events from overwriting newer entitlement state.
Direct payment links require a verified mapping to the same RevenueCat customer and Firebase UID before production release.
Traps and schools are intentionally public. Personal data and moderation metadata must not be stored in those documents.

remainingRisks: Deploy Functions before rules that require the backend-managed admin claim.
Register and monitor valid App Check tokens before enabling enforcement for additional Firebase products.
Add business-level request quotas and abuse monitoring for comments and reports.
Configure the RevenueCat webhook authorization value and monitor failed deliveries.
Verify Stripe-to-RevenueCat identity mapping before releasing web checkout.
Protect backend service accounts with least-privilege IAM and MFA.
